title: Prevent Leaks By Vacation Proofing Your Plumbing
desc: San Antonio plumbing experts explain how to find the shutoff valve, use leak sensors & prepare outdoor faucets for your time away from home.

blocks.text: Leaving town for summer vacation should not mean worrying about leaks or water damage while you are away. A few plumbing checks before you leave can help reduce the risk of coming home to a mess. Water heaters, supply lines, shutoff valves, and outdoor plumbing all deserve attention before the house sits empty. Most of these checks take very little time and can prevent major frustration later.

San Antonio, TX homeowners often leave for several days during the summer travel season. That creates a problem if a leak develops and nobody notices it. Even a slow drip can damage cabinets, flooring, drywall, and insulation after several days. Preparing your plumbing system before a trip helps lower that risk.

At Rosenberg Plumbing & Air, we help homeowners throughout San Antonio and nearby communities prepare plumbing systems for vacations and extended absences. Before you lock the door and head out of town, it’s helpful to review a few key plumbing areas.
Locate and Test the Main Water Shutoff Valve

Your main water shutoff valve controls water entering the house. If a pipe bursts, or a supply line fails, this valve can prevent stop serious damage. Many homeowners do not think about it until an emergency arises. That delay can make a plumbing problem much worse.

Before leaving town, locate the shutoff valve, and confirm that it turns properly. In many houses, you can find the shutoff valve near the water meter, the garage, or an exterior wall. Older valves sometimes stick because of corrosion or mineral buildup. A valve that barely moves may not help much during an emergency.
Some homeowners choose to shut the main water supply off completely when taking longer trips. This is especially helpful if nobody will be checking the property while you are away.
Adjust the Water Heater Before Vacation

Your water heater does not need to maintain full operating temperatures while the house is empty. Lowering the setting can reduce unnecessary energy use during vacation. Many newer systems include a vacation mode for this purpose. That setting helps conserve energy while keeping the system protected.

If your system does not have a vacation setting, check the manufacturer’s recommendations. Gas and electric systems may have different adjustment guidelines. You should avoid shutting some systems down completely unless the manufacturer recommends it. Incorrect shutdown procedures can create startup problems later.

Before leaving, check for warning signs around the water heater itself. Water near the base, rust around fittings, or unusual popping noises may point to a developing problem. Relief valve discharge can also signal excess pressure inside the tank.
A small water heater leak can create major damage in an empty house. If the appliance already shows signs of wear, schedule service before your trip instead of waiting until you return.
Inspect Supply Lines and Plumbing Fixtures

Many plumbing leaks begin in small areas that homeowners rarely inspect closely. Supply lines under sinks, behind toilets, and near appliances can slowly weaken over time. Check your washing machine hoses, refrigerator water lines, and dishwasher connections before vacation. A small leak can spread quietly while the house sits empty.

Check for damp cabinets, soft flooring, rust, mineral buildup, or discoloration near valves and fittings. Around toilets, watch for moisture near the base or a tank that refills too often. Under sinks, inspect supply lines and drain connections carefully. These small clues often appear before larger leaks develop.

If your kitchen sink includes a garbage disposal, inspect the cabinet underneath it carefully. Disposal seals and drain connections can leak slowly over time. Lingering moisture and musty odors may point to a hidden plumbing issue.
You do not need to disassemble anything during these checks. If something already appears damaged, damp, or unreliable, ask us to address it before you travel.
Use Leak Sensors for Additional Protection

Leak sensors provide an extra layer of protection during vacations. These small devices detect water near plumbing fixtures and appliances. Some models sound an alarm inside the home. Others send alerts directly to your phone through a mobile app.

Leak sensors work well near water heaters, sinks, washing machines, refrigerators, and dishwashers. Houses with previous plumbing problems may benefit from additional sensors in crawl spaces or utility rooms. The earlier moisture is detected, the better your chance of limiting damage.
Leak sensors cannot stop water automatically unless you pair them with a shutoff system. However, they can still provide valuable early warning while you are away.
Do Not Forget Outdoor Plumbing and Irrigation

Homeowners often overlook outdoor plumbing before vacations. In San Antonio, summer heat increases irrigation use and outdoor water demand. A leaking hose bib or broken sprinkler head can waste large amounts of water while nobody is home. Water pooling around the foundation can also create drainage concerns.

Inspect outdoor faucets for dripping or leaking around handles and hose connections. Disconnect hoses that you will not be using while you are gone. You should also check your irrigation systems for broken heads, poor spray patterns, or constant dripping. Small irrigation leaks can quietly continue for days.

If your irrigation controller runs automatically, review the watering schedule before leaving. Seasonal weather changes may require adjustments. This is especially important during periods of heavy rain or watering restrictions.
Prepare Your Home for Someone Else to Check

If someone will check your home during vacation, make plumbing information easy to access. Show them where the main shut-off valve is. Point out the water heater and any areas with previous plumbing issues. If you have leak sensors installed, explain what alerts may look or sound like.

This helps neighbors, house sitters, or family members watching your home respond faster if something changes. Many plumbing issues become more manageable when you identify them early. Even a quick walk-through can uncover unusual sounds, odors, or visible moisture.

It also helps to leave access clear around important plumbing equipment. Avoid stacking storage boxes around shutoff valves or water heaters before leaving town. Easy access can matter during an emergency.
Simple Vacation Plumbing Prep Can Prevent Bigger Problems

Vacation plumbing preparation does not need to become overwhelming. Checking the main shutoff valve, adjusting the water heater, inspecting supply lines, and reviewing outdoor plumbing can lower the chance of serious water damage. Leak sensors can also provide valuable peace of mind while you are away from home.
